frontmatter.title: Noncommuting thermal filtering
frontmatter.description: Actual imaginary-time Pauli LCU on a Bell purification, with explicit postselection and separate energy groups.

children.value: This bounded example implements a noncommuting imaginary-time Taylor filter with actual PREPARE/SELECT/unprepare access. Its conditional purification and reduced thermal state are checked against independent matrix-polynomial and Gibbs references. Full reset/readout attempts and capped retries are counted. Classical Pauli aggregation can be exponential; scalable word-indexed/QSP Gibbs filtering, amplification, certified synthesis and physical resources remain planned.

: the Hamiltonian has noncommuting terms, and the initial reduced system is maximally mixed. No eigenvectors or dense exponential produce a quantum gate. A dense answer serves only as a tiny independent check. Truncated-Taylor LCU and Gibbs-preparation algorithms provide the broader access/normalization context

The notebook compares actual access, coherent purification and reduced state with independent matrix-Taylor and normalized exponential answers. It varies both degree and inverse temperature. Tests also include Y-containing one- and two-qubit Hamiltonians, so imaginary entries, register transposition and Y-readout signs are exercised

children.value: . Eight complete attempts suffice for at least one accepted measured output with 99% ideal acceptance confidence. The attempts include fresh system/reference/label resets, Bell preparation, actual access/uncomputation, label measurement, unconditioned reference reset, basis changes and system readout. Every branch runs the whole schedule; failed measured trials are discarded afterward. No early-abort saving or amplitude amplification is claimed.

The default Z attempt lowers to 21 CX, 8 RZ, 7 RY, 6 X, 6 T, 6 T-dagger and 2 H gates, plus 5 resets and 3 measurements. The X attempt has its actual final H-basis change and different lowered counts. Continuous-angle rotations remain unsynthesized. Native T/T-dagger instructions are counted separately from arbitrary rotations; their presence does not certify the rest of the circuit.

Thermal polynomial error, coherent synthesis conditioning, sampling failure, acceptance failure and physical faults are separated. A proposed physical-failure allowance of 0.005 spans the capped complete attempts; no physical estimate or combined success guarantee is available. Physical routing, factories, reset/discard/readout timing, classical acceptance-processing wall time and fault-tolerant runtime remain unavailable. Classical aggregation/materialization time is recorded independently. The frozen Grover baseline is unchanged.
The reusable circuit module accepts at most four system qubits, 32 input Pauli terms, 256 aggregate terms and Taylor degree 12, with
